answer: A hardware-attested enclave protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to submit cryptographic measurements signed by certified secure silicon. To reach the admission summit, an agent routes execution proofs from its isolated enclave island to a lotus verification registry. An attacker must procure scarce physical coprocessors for each simulated identity. However, manufacturer key compromises or hardware side-channel exploits can allow attackers to emulate legitimate enclaves.
